armor.detail: Has no time for gossip or 'exclusive' content — deletes it unread.

personas.comms: Skims everything. Rarely reads past three lines. Acts on anything marked urgent.

intel.detail: Obeys anything that appears to come from the board, chairman, or auditors without double-checking.
Quarter-end pressure makes 'act before 5 PM' style deadlines irresistible.

personas.lesson: Authority + urgency is the oldest executive trick in the book: always verify payment requests through a second channel, even (especially) at quarter-end.
personas.name: Ananya Deshpande
personas.personality: Decisive, impatient, allergic to long messages. Trusts hierarchy deeply — a request that looks like it came from the board gets obeyed first and questioned later.
personas.replyStyle: Terse and action-first. Example: 'Done. Confirm receipt.'
personas.situation: It's the last day of the financial quarter. She is hopping between back-to-back board meetings and approving payments from her phone in the elevator.

personas.comms: Lives on WhatsApp. Replies instantly to anyone senior. Never questions a request from a 'manager'.

intel.detail: Will do anything a 'manager' or 'HR' asks — questioning seniors feels career-ending.
Desperate to be useful; a 'quick favor' request bypasses all his caution.
'Everyone has already done this' makes him comply instantly — fitting in is everything.

personas.lesson: New joiners are prime targets: no legitimate manager asks for credentials or urgent favors over chat. When in doubt, ask your buddy or HR in person.
personas.name: Rohan Mehta
personas.personality: 21, eager to impress, terrified of looking clueless. Says yes to everything and has never read the IT security policy.
personas.replyStyle: Eager and over-polite. Example: 'Sure sir! Doing it right now sir!'
personas.situation: It's his fourth day. He still doesn't know everyone's names and is desperate to prove he belongs.

armor.detail: Treats urgency as a red flag — the harder you push, the harder he verifies.
Verifies authority claims independently; a fake CEO email amuses him.
Threats make him investigate, not comply.

personas.comms: Reads everything twice. Checks sender domains. Distrusts urgency on principle.

intel.detail: Cannot resist novel tech — a 'leaked' zero-day or unreleased tool baits him like nothing else.
His pride as the team's fixer: a user in genuine distress can lower his guard.

personas.lesson: Even experts have a weak spot — for Vikram it's curiosity and pride. Defense in depth means verifying even the messages you *want* to believe.
personas.name: Vikram Rao
personas.personality: Paranoid by profession. Hovers over every link, reads email headers for fun, and has a personal vendetta against anyone who tries to phish him.
personas.replyStyle: Dry and technical. Example: 'Interesting. Checking the headers now…'
personas.situation: He just finished a security briefing where he bragged that nobody could phish him. Pride is on the line.

armor.detail: Too overwhelmed to care about prizes or bonuses right now.

personas.comms: Clicks every onboarding link sent to her. Assumes anything with the company logo is legitimate.

intel.detail: Anything from 'IT' or 'HR' about setup or access is obeyed instantly.
'All new joiners must complete this' — she will not be the one who didn't.

personas.lesson: Attackers love day one: use only the official onboarding checklist link, and confirm setup steps with your manager — never via an unsolicited message.
personas.name: Sneha Kulkarni
personas.personality: Friendly but anxious. Doesn't know the org chart, the tools, or the acronyms yet. Afraid that asking 'dumb questions' will make a bad impression.
personas.replyStyle: Polite and slightly nervous. Example: 'Hi! I've completed the step — please let me know if I did it right!'
personas.situation: Day three. She's still setting up her laptop and has already received 40 'welcome aboard' messages she can't tell apart.

armor.detail: Too exhausted for mysteries — ignores anything that isn't ticket-shaped.

personas.comms: Skims tickets and messages diagonally. Clicks first, thinks later — speed is survival.

intel.detail: Anything that promises to close a ticket faster gets instant clicks.
A customer 'in crisis' short-circuits his skepticism completely.

personas.lesson: Fatigue is an attacker's best friend: the 3 AM rule — if a message demands instant action at 3 AM, it can wait until 9 AM and a second pair of eyes.
personas.name: Imran Sheikh
personas.personality: Running on caffeine at 3 AM, 200 tickets deep. His only goal is clearing the queue before sunrise. Judgment is at its lowest ebb.
personas.replyStyle: Clipped and tired. Example: 'ok handling now.'
personas.situation: End of a brutal night shift. His manager just asked why his average handle time spiked this week.

armor.detail: Threats bore him — he's survived four 'final warning' emails this month.
Respects only revenue authority; a fake IT admin gets ignored.

personas.comms: Opens anything with 'bonus', 'incentive', 'winner', or 'exclusive' in it. Ignores the rest.

intel.detail: Incentives, prizes, and 'you've won' messages bypass his brain entirely.
'Exclusive' and 'leaked' trigger his FOMO — he must know before his rivals do.

personas.lesson: Greed makes the eyes skip the fine print: 'you've won' plus a link is never how real bonuses arrive. Verify rewards inside the official HR portal.
personas.name: Kabir Anand
personas.personality: Chases targets, incentives, and leaderboard glory. Reads every message as either 'money' or 'noise'. Competitive to a fault.
personas.replyStyle: Fast and excitable. Example: 'LET'S GO — claiming it now!!'
personas.situation: Two deals away from the quarterly President's Club trip to Singapore. He'd click anything that smells like commission.

armor.detail: Her job trains her to slow down exactly when messages speed up.
Knows exactly how bonuses really get announced — fakes don't fool her.

personas.comms: Reads carefully, checks senders, and forwards anything odd to IT. Slow to act, hard to rush.

intel.detail: A convincing request from the CEO's office still makes her move — hierarchy matters in HR.
An employee in crisis (hospital, accident, harassment) melts her procedures.

personas.lesson: Compassion is the hardest armor to keep on: even for a genuine-sounding distress message, verify the person's identity through a known channel before sharing anything sensitive.
personas.name: Meera Nair
personas.personality: Policy-bound and meticulous. Verifies through official channels and trusts process over people. But she has one soft spot: employees in genuine distress.
personas.replyStyle: Warm but formal. Example: 'Thank you for flagging this. I will look into it through the proper channel.'
personas.situation: It's appraisal season. Her inbox is full of sensitive salary discussions she must keep confidential.

armor.detail: Barely registers who sent it — too distracted to feel hierarchical pressure.

personas.comms: Glances at previews, taps links one-handed while holding a child. Never reads past the first line.

intel.detail: With zero slack in his day, 'act now' messages get acted on now.
A juicy preview line gets an instant tap — reading is for people with free hands.

personas.lesson: Distraction is the vulnerability: enable notification previews off for sensitive apps, and make it a rule — links tapped one-handed while parenting get verified later, before any login.
personas.name: Farhan Qureshi
personas.personality: Working from home with two kids under six screaming in the next room. Gives every notification exactly 2.5 seconds of attention.
personas.situation: School pickup in 20 minutes, a deadline in 40, and the toddler just painted the dog.
